claims.statement: Alarm ALM-94252 fired for heater_temp_C above 403.0 with value 412.194 on LOT-1239
Heater jumped to 411.99 for LOT-1236 and 412.19 for LOT-1239, up from 400.6 for LOT-1229 and 400.52 for LOT-1230
Thickness after the jump was 511.2 for LOT-1236, up from 499.81 for LOT-1229 and 502.87 for LOT-1230
Nearby lots on the same clean and metrology tools were normal with LOT-1231 at 502.91 and LOT-1238 at 502.01, while LOT-1236 on DEP01-A was at 511.2
DEP01-A stands out with max 511.2 and std 3.27 and n_ooc 1, versus DEP01-B mean 500.79 std 1.32 and DEP02-B mean 501.74 std 1.21

disposition.summary: Heater on DEP01-A jumped hot starting at LOT-1236 and stayed hot for the alarm lot. The wafer processed right after the jump came out much thicker, matching a real temperature rise. Hold the alarm lot and the chamber.

public: Plummer, Deal, Griffin, course notes for Silicon VLSI Technology, ch. 9 (thin film deposition)
In the reaction-limited regime CVD deposition rate follows an Arrhenius law and is very temperature sensitive.
sources.practitioner: A real temperature change shows up in the film on wafers processed after it; a sensor fault does not.
